# Cīvarakkhandhaka (Kd 8)
**ID:** Kd 8
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Cīvarakkhandhaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-kd8
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m2.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Cīvarakkhandhaka* ("The chapter on robes" or "the Chapter on robe-cloth") is the eighth Khandhaka of the Pali *Vinaya Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral; Prebish 1994]. The text lays down extensive legislation regarding robes, robe-material, dyeing equipment, and the inheritance and distribution of a deceased monk's personal belongings [SuttaCentral; Schopen 1997]. It frames these regulations around notable narrative cycles, including the biography of Jīvaka Komārabhacca (the Buddha's physician, born in Pali tradition to the courtesan Sālavatī of Rājagaha), interactions with King Bimbisāra and Prince Abhaya, and the lay disciple Visākhā's requests regarding robe donations and requisites [SuttaCentral; Banerjee 1979]. It also contains the story of the Buddha and Ānanda personally washing and nursing a monk suffering from dysentery [SuttaCentral]. In treating the death of monks, the chapter legitimizes the formal distribution of the deceased's monastic estate, robes being among the primary forms of personal monastic property [Schopen 1997].
Direct parallels to the chapter exist across other Vinaya recensions, notably the *Cīvaravastu* of the Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition preserved in Sanskrit and Tibetan, alongside counterparts in the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka Vinayas [SuttaCentral; Frauwallner 1956; Prebish 1994]. A. C. Banerjee notes that the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda version closely parallels the Pali narrative framework and rules on inheritance, while elaborating stories such as Jīvaka's birth and the tales of Upananda and Mṛgaśīrṣa [Banerjee 1979]. Passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include the *Muṭṭhassatisutta* (AN 5.210) and multiple rules of the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas (Bu-Vb Np 1, Bi-Vb Pc 21, Bi-Vb Pc 22) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus strongly aligns the text with the Sanskrit *Cīvaravastu* and Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (confirming SuttaCentral's curated parallels), and highlights widespread Pali-internal reuse across other Khandhakas (such as the *Senāsana-*, *Bhesajja-*, and *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka*), the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5 and AN 8), and the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16) [DharmaNexus]. Complete English translations include those by T. W. Rhys Davids and Hermann Oldenberg, I. B. Horner, and Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral; Prebish 1994].
